allec-oavg.disclosure: Measured on the 27 Oct 2026 draw and shown unranked until that draw is equated to the reference scale. First measurement of the allec-oavg configuration at plantwaterer/allec revision e54027aa1f865bdd25724e9b3c1acb51b2bbc3c3 on this draw. Serving description: same weights as the earlier allec entry; short requests are read in several option orders and averaged. (The allec weights are plantwaterer/allec@e54027aa; no separate allec row is published on this board.) The author's own decision library is invoked through a first-party loopback HTTP shim. Choice and noul return native probabilities; score is unsupported. Each choice item is read once per option order (four reads); all forwarded prompts are counted in the processed tokens and in cost. Averaging is native inference, with no extra host ensemble, generated reasoning or answer repair. Text only. The native 32,768-token forward limit requires full normalized state; no raised cap or truncation. Successful public probes through 4,096 tokens establish those probes only. Of 1,500 requests, 1,120 answered and 380 returned preregistered HTTP 422 refusals for unsupported score criteria or context/state-shown limits. Refusals remain misses where their question type is supported; unsupported score questions follow the frozen scorer's supported-type rule. The scored set contains 1,125 supported-type items: the 375 unsupported score questions are excluded, while five supported-type refusals count as misses. There were no native deviations. Processed input: 739,884 expanded-prefill tokens, matching the independent offline count, with zero generated output and zero usage mismatches. The scored loop took 208.734721660614 s. Displayed self-hosted latency is an estimate under the shared method, not a measured hosted endpoint. Replay: 50 requests, 33 byte-identical, zero argmax flips and reported maximum probability difference 0.0; this does not establish byte-identical agreement on every request. Post-run health was ready. The model card declares Apache-2.0; no LICENSE file ships in the repository. The card's own training inventory lists corpora under non-commercial, copyleft or research-only terms (e.g. XNLI/translation data). Whether the Apache-2.0 declaration covers that training data is the author's claim and is unverified; commercial use should review the training-data terms. The Decision Index excludes two of its private new-domain tests for this model, reporting signs its training data overlapped them (the lab's claim, carried as such). No JevBench contamination audit was run; there is no evidence of training on JevBench items. Displayed with a non-commercial-style restriction label; this does not establish unrestricted commercial rights. The measured device was one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 96 GB, not an established minimum. This is the completed single-row run for this configuration on this draw, with no scored retry or response repair. Usage, native-deviation, replay and health checks do not alter scored responses.
allec-oavg.endpoint_condition: Measured 30 Oct 2026 on an evaluator-owned Verda VM in FIN-03 (Finland, EU), one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, nominal 96 GB, image 24.04.cuda13.0. THE AUTHOR'S OWN MODEL AND DECISION LIBRARY, with a first-party loopback System One wire shim: plantwaterer/allec at e54027aa1f865bdd25724e9b3c1acb51b2bbc3c3. Library-only submission, with no author HTTP server. The shim calls the author's unchanged README entry point LenAvgBayesEngine(model=local_model, device=cuda) from lenavg_bayes_engine; it does not substitute the older single-pass DikitEngine. Full Gemma-4-31B-derived weights and trained decision head are measured together. Native defaults remain BF16 backbone, CPU FP64 L01-post head, bidirectional global jev_mem attention and causal sliding layers, max_len 32,768, tokens_per_batch 32,768, l_star 939 and averaging enabled. Short-request routing uses structural characters, not token counts. Native four-order choice averaging for menus of at most 52 options, two-order noul averaging, deterministic author temperatures and Bayesian head correction are retained. Menus above 52 retain native chunk scoring, model-selected finalists and the final round, including total 0.001 probability mass on discarded final options. Requests are serialized because native forward hooks and averaging flags are mutable. Native probabilities are transported unchanged; no generated text, host retry, answer repair, stock causal generation, quantization or stock-vLLM equivalence. Score criteria are unsupported: the shim returns native-domain HTTP 422 before the author's length helper can hit .items() on score-list criteria, without score-to-choice conversion. Native context/state-shown refusals also return HTTP 422. No truncation, raised context cap, split state or fallback inference. The native renderer's crop followed by check_state_shown is transcribed as a refusal before forwarding. The first-party observer additionally refuses any alternative forward missing the full normalized state or exceeding 32,768 tokens; this is a disclosed no-truncation transport adaptation. Structured state uses native JSON conversion, preserving native structural-length routing on the original state. USAGE IS FIRST-PARTY OBSERVED ACCOUNTING: numeric input_tokens sums the tokenizer lengths of every actually forwarded prompt, including averaged option orders, packed sequences and second rounds; it is expanded prefill, not a single read and not an author-native billing contract. Output_tokens is 0 because no continuation is generated. The frozen TypeSafe adapter and measurement driver remain unchanged, including the 120 s transport timeout. Decision Index base.py is pinned at 9eb2dbe2a358004c8782c66e40a83ac07b953fec; no Decision Index suite or training code runs. Runtime receipts retain source, package RECORD and tokenizer hashes; torch 2.14.1, CUDA 13.0, transformers 5.12.1, tokenizers 0.22.2, numpy 2.2.6, safetensors 0.8.0 and accelerate 1.15.0. Source review found no benchmark-item answer lookup in the serving closure; framework internals were not exhaustively audited. Author code and weights ran only on the disposable rented pod, with verified local artifacts, read-only mounts, empty credentials, offline flags and network cut before sealed input. Separate public warm-ups preceded three fresh timed repetitions each at 256 and 2,048 tokens and two at 4,096. Native typed probes passed, including 255-choice, Unicode JSON and structural-routing boundaries. Unsupported score and over-limit probes returned HTTP 422. These are synthetic observations, not scored latency aggregates. Separate public pre-warm passed. The complete 1,500-request run took 208.734721660614 s; raw output sha256 185c8f534d2e8b21d38a39af9a3152f0f4754c41bf921128bb4d2b768698aee7 was verified. Post-run health was ready. The VM was closed and temporary node and local copies deleted, with no cleanup errors reported. GPU rental spend is separate from the benchmark's model-cost estimate.

zils-ai-z3-mini-soup-preview.disclosure: Measured on the 27 Oct 2026 draw and shown unranked until that draw is equated to the reference scale. z3-mini-soup-preview is Zils AI's 4.5B decision-model merge at 1492185bb48347db2a9d88f8bf18cb0e9c17a55b, distinct from its ingredients and from the author's current z3-mini release. The pinned author README describes a uniform average of THREE decision models sharing Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B at 851bf6e806efd8d0a36b00ddf55e13ccb7b8cd0a: torchcast-ai/torchcast-decision-4b at 492bfb19662f3c6e601cc9c4bd2911ac95609ed4, perplexity-ai/pplx-decider-flash-v1.2 at 9ff7cf9838e59df461c276b7699d56b244d2af58 and vllm-sr/d3-mini at df99bf4ca4418bc6908ee68e9b7479af1f3b8800. Qwen is their shared base, not a fourth soup ingredient. According to that README, language_model.* and visual.* weights are uniformly averaged in FP32 and saved BF16; the answer layer is stated to be byte-identical to d3-mini, with tokenizer, prompt and runtime unchanged. These are the author's provenance claims; no tensor-content comparison was performed. The author's own native serving path was measured on rented hardware. Choice, noul and score return native probabilities without generated answer text or reasoning. Text only; image and video were not measured. CONFIGURATION DISCLOSURE: The soup's model.json profile (d3-mini-4.5b-v1, max_input_tokens: 8192) describes a different packaged profile, and the retained NOTICE-torchcast describes the torchcast_decision package's 16,384-token head/tail truncation, yes/no commit floor 0.801 and T=0.9. These settings are not read or applied by the selected native d3 runtime. Text inspection of pinned d3_runtime.py/d3_server.py finds no model.json or NOTICE-torchcast read and no torchcast commit-floor implementation. Native configuration is decision_config.json (max_length: null, temperature: 1.0); the native health response reports max_input_tokens null. No 8192/16384 cap, truncation or commit floor applies on this serving path. No configured input-length cap and no truncation; the preregistered refusal set was empty. Offline count: 1,500 items, 964,081 input tokens and maximum answered input 80,357 tokens. Successful public native and frozen-adapter probes through 81,965 tokens establish those probes only, not unlimited context. All 1,500 requests answered with zero refusals, zero errors and zero native deviations, without scored retry. Processed input: 964,081 measured server input tokens, equal to the offline count with zero mismatches; output zero. Five decisions exceeded 10 s and were answered; this observation does not change native completion accounting or selectively exclude items. Under the ten-second rule, the five decisions above ten seconds count as wrong answers. Scored loop: 110.09967112541199 s. Displayed self-hosted latency is an estimate under the shared method, not a measured hosted endpoint. Replay: 50 requests, 50 bit-identical, zero argmax flips and maximum absolute probability difference 0.0. Warm-up preceded timed public probes, the scored server passed a separate public pre-warm and post-run health was ready. Apache-2.0 is declared for the soup, shared base and three ingredients; LICENSE, LICENSE-pplx, LICENSE-torchcast, LICENSE-qwen-Apache-2.0, NOTICE, NOTICE-pplx and NOTICE-torchcast were retained. The card discloses possible third-party benchmark overlap. We did not inspect training data or verify overlap with JevBench public or sealed items; no clean-training claim is made. Zils' private exam figures are self-reported and are neither JevBench nor Decision Index measurements. One completed scored run on this draw; usage, native-deviation, replay, health and long-latency checks do not alter scored responses.
